enkf_watersim.label: Ensemble Kalman filter on WaterSim (HBV + snow), joint state-parameter
enkf_watersim.numpy_only_reason: runs the vendored WaterSim kernels (HBV step, degree-day snow) inside a numba-compiled filter loop; numba compiles at first call (~3 s), no cache files written (cache=False). A pure-numpy port would be ~100x slower (daily loop x 32 members x 4,000+ days).

compute.notes: No network training. 0.64 CPU-h tuning filter settings on 250 simulated TRAIN runs (tools/tune.py, ~75 variants, work/tune/*.jsonl) + 0.32 CPU-h rung evaluations (4 rungs + an open-loop diagnostic; 800 sim val runs + 52 dev basins x 3 leads) + ~0.02 smoke tests. One thread, nice 5.

enkf_watersim.feature_engineering: No learned features. Uses forcing columns P, PET, T_mean; the 11 attributes -> a WaterSim basin spec (elevation bands from mean and range, slope, forest, porosity, ksat, carbonate, urban; aridity and p_mean from the static vector) -> WaterSim's attribute transfer functions for HBV + degree-day snow parameters and the p1 water-yield multiplier prior (elevation, frac_snow, p_mean); observed flow qobs up to the forecast origin (t - lead) is assimilated as log(Q + c), c = 0.02 x p_mean.

enkf_watersim_conformal.label: Ensemble Kalman filter on WaterSim (HBV + snow), joint state-parameter + Mondrian conformal
enkf_watersim_conformal.numpy_only_reason: wraps enkf_watersim: runs the vendored WaterSim kernels (HBV step, degree-day snow) inside a numba-compiled filter loop; numba compiles at first call (~3 s), no cache files written (cache=False). A pure-numpy port would be ~100x slower (daily loop x 32 members x 4,000+ days).

compute.notes: conformal fit only (dev predictions of enkf_watersim + shifts); the base arm is not retrained

enkf_watersim_conformal.feature_engineering: none beyond enkf_watersim's; the conformal offset uses static[11] (mean forcing P) and the class list (strata)

tab_dpl.label: Decides through physics: MLP -> WaterSim HBV parameters, trained through the simulator
tab_dpl.family_label: Differentiable simulator / physics in the loop
tab_dpl.numpy_only_reason: The prediction IS a WaterSim run: predict.py maps attributes to parameters with a numpy MLP and then calls the harness's vendored WaterSim (numba-compiled HBV + degree-day snow + gamma channel UH + irrigation) through wsim.py. Re-writing WaterSim in numpy would duplicate the simulator the arm is meant to use.

compute.notes: One thread (process_time). torch-vs-WaterSim verification 25 s; two aborted pilot runs of the base (NSE* loss 336 s, log(1+NSE*) loss 558 s: both drove the volume bias to ~0.75); r0 0.745 h; r1 0.819 h; r2 0.425 h; band fitting + exports ~25 s. Harness evaluation ~1 min per rung.

tab_dpl.feature_engineering: Network input: the 18-value static vector as given, standardised with the sim-train mean/sd. The simulator input: the batch forcing (P x the learned PMULT, PET from the forcing, T_mean) and a spec built from the attributes (area, elevation mean +- range/2 -> 5 equal-area bands, slope, irrigation share, lat/lon); spin-up = the 365 warm-up rows. Nothing else.

tab_dpl_conformal.numpy_only_reason: wraps tab_dpl: The prediction IS a WaterSim run: predict.py maps attributes to parameters with a numpy MLP and then calls the harness's vendored WaterSim (numba-compiled HBV + degree-day snow + gamma channel UH + irrigation) through wsim.py. compute.notes: One thread (process_time). Symbolic search 251 s (17 parameters x 50 s wall each; lawsearch.py vendored unchanged from LawFinder); r1 constant tuning through the torch simulator 613 s; band fitting + exports 3 x ~8 s. The teacher mapping is arm tab_dpl r1 (its 2.25 CPU h are counted there, not here).

tab_formula.feature_engineering: Formula inputs: the 18 raw static-vector values (log_area, elev_mean_km, elev_range_km, log_slope_mkm, forest_frac, soil_porosity, log_ksat_cmh, carbonate_frac, reservoir_frac, irrigation_frac, urban_frac, log_p_mean, pet_mean, log_aridity, frac_snow, hp_freq, lp_freq, t_mean_c). Simulator input as tab_dpl: batch forcing (P x PMULT, PET, T_mean) and a spec from the attributes; spin-up = the 365 warm-up rows.

tab_gbm.label: Gradient-boosted trees (LightGBM -> numpy trees)

compute.notes: One thread (process_time). Feature tables 7 s + 15 s + 15 s + 20 s reorder; a failed first launch (LightGBM refuses monotone constraints with the quantile objective) ~125 s; r0 223 s; r1 609 s; r2 221 s; r3 289 s. Six boosters per rung (mean + 5 quantiles). Harness evaluation (not training) used another ~0.8 CPU h over the 4 rungs.

tab_gbm.feature_engineering: Per day, from the batch forcing + static vector only (feats.py): P(t+1), P(t), P(t-1), P(t-2), sum P(t-6..t-3); liquid input W = rain + melt of a fixed one-band degree-day snow proxy (TT 0 C, 2 C interval, 3 mm/C/day) at t, t-1, t-2 and melt(t); EMAs of W over 3, 10, 30, 90, 365 days; two bucket models (50 and 300 mm: fill fraction, spill EMA, drain) and a 60-day linear store; T(t), EMA10 T, PET(t), EMA30 PET; SWE proxy, log1p(SWE); sin/cos day of year; the 18-value static vector. Water features and the target are divided by p_mean (the forcing's mean precipitation); target = qo / p_mean. 47 features.

tab_gp.label: Sparse Gaussian process (SGPR, 500 inducing points, scoped features)

compute.notes: One thread (process_time). r0 652 s; r1 732 s; r2 724 s; r3 1266 s (hyperparameter + inducing-input optimisation with the collapsed bound on 20,000 rows, then the posterior over 200,000 rows). Shares the sim-train feature table of tab_gbm (7 s to build).

tab_gp.feature_engineering: SCOPED subset (20 of tab_gbm's 47 daily features, feats.py, from the batch forcing + static vector only): P(t+1), P(t), liquid input W(t), W(t-1), melt(t) of a one-band degree-day snow proxy, EMAs of W over 3/10/30/90/365 days, two bucket fill fractions and spills, a 60-day slow store, EMA10 T, EMA30 PET, log1p SWE proxy, log aridity, snow fraction. Water features and target divided by p_mean; target transform z = sqrt(qo / p_mean). Inputs standardised with the training mean/sd.
